implementation.compatibility_classification: IBM TSO/E and VM non-SAA extension; POS(needle,haystack[,start]) remains the portable preferred function.
implementation.approach: INDEX calls the shared POS byte-search core with the first two string arguments reversed. No second search engine or recursive public dispatch was introduced.
implementation.byte_semantics: Exact case-sensitive byte comparison; embedded NUL, high-bit, nonprintable, and all 00-FF byte values are preserved.
implementation.limits: Existing 16 MiB string limit retained. No Unicode, locale, or DBCS behavior added.
implementation.start_validation: Optional positive whole REXX decimal, default 1; exact parsing and validation precede offset calculation. Valid positive starts beyond the string, including values above UINT32_MAX, return 0.
implementation.pos_compatibility_correction: Prior POS conversion returned RESOURCE_LIMIT for valid positive starts above UINT32_MAX. Since all supported strings are shorter, RX26 now returns 0 for such starts in the shared POS and INDEX core; direct regression cases cover both names.
implementation.input_mutation: None; input views are borrowed, and the existing result-construction helper is used.

inventory_preflight.pos_status: Implemented; one-byte-oriented POS search was present.

RX26 staged that same script under a shorter RX26-only name; the complete retry passed. The failed attempt's uncaptured QAC parent exit status is recorded as unknown in its attempt evidence.
